question.worked_solution:
We break up the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{2}{1+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{2}{1+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{2}{1+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Evaluating the first of these integrals, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{2}{1+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =2{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}\frac{1}{1+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }(2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2x){|}_{a}^{0}) \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\operatorname{arctan}⁡0-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(2a)) \\  & =0-(-\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the integrand is an **even** function. This means that we can immediately deduce that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{2}{1+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{2}{1+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{2}{1+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{2}{1+4{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
